words.gloss: five; roots; pañcamūla = a group of five roots (the five roots are not named in this unit)
bilva (Aegle marmelos, bael; standard); beginning with, and the rest

hindi: पञ्चमूल से साधित तैल, अथवा बिल्व यानी बेल आदि से साधित।
english: Oil prepared with the five roots (pañcamūla), or with bilva (bael) and the rest.
notes: Elliptical: 'sādhitam' (prepared) is read with both instruments 'pañcamūlena' and 'bilvādinā'. bilva = Aegle marmelos (standard); the Hindi name is bel. 'bilvādi' is read literally as 'bilva and the rest' without naming the members. Which oil and which enema it serves is not stated here (compare 119).

hindi: अनुवासन श्लेष्म को हरने वाला, अथवा कफ का नाश करने वाले द्रव्यों से।
english: An anuvāsana (oil enema) that removes phlegm (śleṣman), or one with substances that destroy Kapha.
notes: Elliptical: no verb is given; the line states what kind of anuvāsana (or with what substances) is meant. 'dravyaiḥ ... kaphaghātibhiḥ' is an instrumental 'with Kapha-destroying substances'. anuvāsana is the oil (unctuous) enema (standard).

hindi: कफ में फलों के साथ और आठ गुने खट्टे में पकाया हुआ अन्वासन।
english: In Kapha, an anvāsana (oil enema) cooked with fruits and in the eightfold sour (amla).
notes: 'aṣṭaguṇe amle' is rendered literally 'in the eightfold sour'; the noun to which 'sour' belongs (a liquid?) and what is eightfold (the measure?) are not stated. 'anvāsana' is a variant spelling of anuvāsana (see 119). The line is a phrase without a main verb.

hindi: शूल और आनाह में उससे युक्त निरूह, अनुमानित पाठ के अनुसार सम्भवतः पटु यानी नमक और मूत्र वाला।
english: In pain (śūla) and distension (ānāha), a nirūha (decoction enema) joined with that, on a conjectural reading having paṭu (probably salt) and urine.

text_flags.why: possible: 'paiṭu' is not a word; 'paṭu' (salt, probable) with mūtra (urine) fits the sense of a nirūha

notes: 'paiṭumūtravān' is not a known word; read as 'paṭu-mūtra-vān' (possible typo, ai for a). paṭu in drug lists is often salt (probable), but this is not firm. 'tadyukta' = joined with that, referring back to the preceding unit's anvāsana (reference not certain). nirūha = decoction enema (standard). Verb not given.

hindi: तब बुद्धिमान् अग्निवेश ने मुनि से इस प्रकार पूछा: यहाँ, परन्तु, फलों में क्या
english: Then the wise Agniveśa asked the sage thus: 'Here, but what, of fruits'
notes: GROUPING: the question continues in 123 ('... may be always beneficial in basti-action?'). 'pṛcchati sma' is the present with sma, giving a past sense. 'iti' here (after munim) is read as 'thus', introducing the question; the question ends at 'syāt' in 123, and the 'iti' after punarvasuḥ in 123 goes with praśaśāsa. 'agniveśa' = agniveśaḥ (visarga dropped before iha).
lines_deva: पृच्छतिस्म मुनिमित्यथ धीमानग्निवेश इह किं तु फलानां
lines_iast: pṛcchatisma munimityatha dhīmānagniveśa iha kiṃ tu phalānāṃ

hindi: बस्तिकर्म में सदा हितकर क्या होगा? उसको पुनर्वसु ने इस प्रकार उपदेश दिया।
english: '... may be always beneficial in basti-action (enema procedure)?' Punarvasu thus instructed him.
notes: GROUPING: completes the question begun in 122. 'taṃ' = him (Agniveśa, from 122). The sage of 122 is named Punarvasu here. 'iti' is placed after 'punarvasuḥ' and read as 'thus'; the answer follows in 124 onward.
lines_deva: बस्तिकर्मणि हितं सततं स्यात्तं पुनर्वसुरिति प्रशशास
lines_iast: bastikarmaṇi hitaṃ satataṃ syāttaṃ punarvasuriti praśaśāsa

words.gloss: kuṣṭha (a group of skin diseases; standard); beneficial
ikṣvāku (probably bitter bottle gourd, Lagenaria siceraria; probable); fruit
for those with prameha (a group of urinary disorders; standard)

hindi: यहाँ, अनुमानित पाठ के अनुसार, गैरागिरी कुष्ठ में हितकर है; प्रमेह वालों के लिए सम्भवतः कड़वी लौकी यानी इक्ष्वाकु का फल हितकर है।
english: Here, on a conjectural reading, gairāgirī (an unclear word) is beneficial in kuṣṭha; for those with prameha the fruit of ikṣvāku (probably bitter bottle gourd) is beneficial.
notes: 'gairāgirī' is not a known name; kept unsplit and unidentified (unidentified). Its femininity is shown by 'hitā'. ikṣvāku = bitter bottle gourd, Lagenaria siceraria (not Momordica; probable). kuṣṭha is read as the skin-disease group, not the drug costus, because 'hitā' goes with a disease context. prameha is rendered as a Sanskrit term (group of urinary disorders, standard).

words.gloss: in pāṇḍu (pale-disease: anaemia with pallor; standard)

hindi: कुटज यानी कुड़ा का फल हृदय के रोग में श्रेष्ठ है, पर कौट फल पाण्डु यानी रक्ताल्पता में।
english: The fruit of kuṭaja (kurchi) is foremost in heart ailment, but the kauṭa-fruit in pāṇḍu (anaemia with pallor).
notes: 'pravaram' is carried over to the second half. 'kauṭaphala' is not identified (unidentified): it may mean 'fruit of kuṭa' or a corrupted form, so it is kept as printed. kuṭaja = Holarrhena antidysenterica (standard).
lines_deva: कुटजस्य फलं हृदामये प्रवरं कौटफलं तु पांडुषु
lines_iast: kuṭajasya phalaṃ hṛdāmaye pravaraṃ kauṭaphalaṃ tu pāṃḍuṣu

words.gloss: kṛtavedhana (probably ridge gourd, Luffa acutangula; probable)

hindi: उदर में कृतवेधन यानी सम्भवतः तोरई हितकर है; मदन यानी मैनफल तो सब रोगों में अविरोधी है।
english: In the belly (udara) kṛtavedhana (probably ridge gourd) is beneficial; madana (emetic nut), however, is not opposed to any disease.
notes: udara is rendered 'belly' per the book glossary; in this context the disease called udara (abdominal enlargement) may be meant. kṛtavedhana is probably Luffa acutangula (probable); madana = Randia dumetorum (standard). 'sarvagadāvirodhi' = 'not opposed to all diseases' (not contrary in any).
lines_deva: उदरे कृतवेधनं हितं मदनं सर्वगदाविरोधि तु
lines_iast: udare kṛtavedhanaṃ hitaṃ madanaṃ sarvagadāvirodhi tu

hindi: मधुर, कसैले और कड़वे के साथ, वह रूखा नहीं, अनुमानित पाठ के अनुसार तीखे, उष्ण और चिपचिपे के साथ।
english: Sweet, with astringent and bitter (ones); that is not dry; on a conjectural reading, with pungent, hot and slimy (ones).

text_flags.why: possible: 'ṭṛṣṇa' (thirst) does not fit a list of qualities; sa-kaṭu-uṣṇa-picchila (pungent, hot, slimy) fits

notes: Subject is madana of 126 (understood). 'sakaṭṛṣṇapicchilaṃ' is printed with 'ṭṛṣṇa' ('thirst'); read as sa-kaṭu-uṣṇa-picchila on a conjectural reading (possible typo: ṭū for ṭṛ). 'kaṣāya' here is the astringent taste.

words.gloss: wind (pavana); going in the natural direction

hindi: जो कफ और पित्त को हरने वाला, शीघ्र काम करने वाला, हानिरहित और वायु का अनुलोमन करने वाला है।
english: Which removes Kapha and Pitta, acts quickly, is harmless, and makes the wind (pavana) move in its natural direction (anuloma).
notes: 'hṛdāśukāri' is split hṛt + āśukāri (hṛt becomes hṛd before ā). Alternative reading 'hṛd' (heart) is not supported by the sentence. Continues the description of madana (126-127).

hindi: इसलिए वह फल आदि में आस्थापन के प्रयोगों में श्रेष्ठ माना गया है।
english: Therefore that is held foremost among fruit and the rest, in applications of āsthāpana (decoction enema).
notes: Closes the answer of Punarvasu. 'phalādiṣu' = among fruit and the rest. āsthāpana is the decoction enema (= nirūha, standard). The closing 'iti' (thus) after yojanāsu is left out of the translations per glossary.

words.gram: past act. part. (-vat) √sthā, m. loc. sg.

hindi: तब मुनिश्रेष्ठ के वचन कहकर रुक जाने पर, उसने फिर निवेदन किया।
english: Then, when the bull among sages (muni-vṛṣabha) had spoken his words and stopped, he again made a request.
notes: The subject of 'vijñāpayāṃ babhūva' is not named in this unit; 131 gives the speaker as bowed down with the other disciples (Agniveśa by context, not stated). 'vijñāpayāṃbabhūva' is the periphrastic perfect 'vijñāpayām babhūva'. 'munivṛṣabha' is an epithet, here for Punarvasu by context.
lines_deva: अथ मुनिवृषभे निगद्य वाक्यं स्थितवति विज्ञापयांबभूव भूयः
lines_iast: atha munivṛṣabhe nigadya vākyaṃ sthitavati vijñāpayāṃbabhūva bhūyaḥ

words.gloss: gone down to the ground, bowed

hindi: यह अत्यन्त गहन; अन्य शिष्यों के साथ भूमि पर झुका हुआ, आगे अञ्जलि रखकर।
english: This very profound (matter): bowed down to the ground together with the other disciples, having placed the joined hands (añjali) in front.

text_flags.why: possible: 'jalim' is not a word; ñ was dropped in print, añjali (joined hands) intended

notes: GROUPING: the sentence is incomplete; it runs into 132 and 133, where the question is stated. The verb is not in this unit. 'idam' (this) is read as the object of the question that follows.

hindi: गुरु के द्वारा विचित्र कर्म और गुण करने वाला कहा गया बस्ति ऊपर जाता है, और नाभि से नहीं।
english: The basti (enema), said by the teacher to produce varied actions and benefits, goes upward then, and not from the navel.
notes: The line is hard: 'ca eti na nābheḥ' is rendered literally ('and goes, not from the navel'); the intended contrast (it goes upward, yet it is applied below the navel) is not stated in the Sanskrit and is not added. 'guṇa' is taken as 'benefit, quality'. The question continues in 133. 'atha' could also be read as a sentence particle.

hindi: और शीघ्र आता है, अनुमानित पाठ के अनुसार अनुस अस्पष्ट, देह से सब ओर से; दोषों को कैसे हटाता है।
english: And quickly arrives, 'anusa' (unclear), from the body on all sides; how does it drive away the doṣas?
notes: GROUPING: completes the question begun in 131-132; the teacher answers from 134. 'cānusa' cannot be restored with certainty (perhaps a sandhi/typo for a word like 'anusṛtya'); kept as printed and glossed unclear; reading is conjectural. 'apohati' is from apa-√ūh (drives away, removes).

hindi: गुरु ने कहा: यह शरीर का, जो बाहर या भीतर आश्रित है, स्तिमित वायु के वश में है।
english: The teacher said: this of the body, whatever is dependent outside or within, is subject to the wind (māruta) that is stimita (still, stagnant).
notes: Difficult line. 'stimitamārutavaśyam' is read as 'subject to still (stagnant) wind'; 'stimita' may also mean 'wet, steady'. 'apāśritam' is read as 'dependent, resting'. The relative 'yat' and the demonstrative 'etat' are not fully resolved; this is a literal reading.

words.gram: pres. part. caus. √jan, m. nom. sg.

words.gloss: unclear (printed form kept); ends in roga-pūgān 'crowds of diseases'

hindi: उस दूषित के अनुलोम भाव को उत्पन्न करता हुआ बस्ति, अनुमानित पाठ के अनुसार अस्पष्ट विषमान्तिरोगपूगान् को नष्ट करता है।
english: Producing the natural direction (anulomatā) in that spoiled (wind), the basti destroys, on a conjectural reading, the 'viṣamāntirogapūgān' (unclear; the end of the word is 'groups of diseases').
notes: 'viṣamāntirogapūgān' is kept unsplit: the first part is damaged (perhaps viṣama-āntara-roga-pūga 'irregular internal groups of diseases', not firm). 'tasya duṣṭasya' is read as the wind of 134 (the wind that is stagnant); noun not stated.
lines_deva: दुष्टस्य तस्य जनयन्ननुलोमतां तु बस्तिर्हिनस्ति विषमान्तिरोगपूगान्
lines_iast: duṣṭasya tasya janayannanulomatāṃ tu bastirhinasti viṣamāntirogapūgān

words.gloss: vital spot (marma); upper; all; parts; limbs; born in

hindi: शाखा में गए और कोष्ठ में गए रोग, और मर्म, ऊर्ध्व, सब अवयवों और अंगों में उत्पन्न होने वाले।
english: Diseases gone to the branches (śākhā) and gone to the storehouse (koṣṭha), and those born in the vital spots (marma), the upper (parts), and all the parts and limbs.
notes: Continues in 137 ('ye santi teṣām'). The compound 'marma-ūrdhva-sarva-avayava-aṅga-ja' is read as a list of locations of origin. śākhā is rendered literally as 'branch'; koṣṭha as 'storehouse'.

hindi: जो हैं, उनके जन्म में वायु से परे कोई और हेतु नहीं है।
english: Those that exist: of them there is no other cause at all, beyond wind (vāyu), in (their) origin.
notes: Refers back to the diseases of 136. 'vāyoḥ param' is read as 'other than, beyond wind'.
lines_deva: ये संति तेषां न तु कश्चिदन्यो वायोः परं जन्मनि हेतुरस्ति
lines_iast: ye saṃti teṣāṃ na tu kaścidanyo vāyoḥ paraṃ janmani heturasti

words.gloss: faeces; drying, wasting (śoṣa); Pitta; and so on; waste (mala); accumulations

hindi: विट्, शोष, पित्त आदि मलों के संचयों का विक्षेप और संहार करने वाला वायु ही है।
english: For wind (vāyu) is the doer of the scattering and the gathering of the accumulations of wastes (mala): faeces, drying (śoṣa), Pitta and so on.
notes: The first compound is hard to divide: 'viṭ-śoṣa-pitta-ādi-mala-ācaya'; it is taken as the accumulations of faeces, śoṣa (drying/wasting), Pitta and other wastes. 'śoṣa' in a list with faeces and Pitta is odd (possible corruption, e.g. of 'śleṣma'); not changed.

hindi: उस अत्यन्त बढ़े हुए के शमन के लिए बस्ति के समान दूसरा कोई औषध नहीं है, क्योंकि
english: For the pacification of that greatly increased (wind) there is no other remedy equal to basti, because

text_flags.why: possible: dative 'śamāya' (for pacification) fits; the final anusvara is a typo

notes: GROUPING: the 'because' clause continues in 140. 'basteḥ' is printed 'vasteḥ' (orthographic va for ba, normalised in `w`). 'śamāyaṃ' has a stray anusvara.
lines_deva: तस्यातिवृद्धस्य शमायं नान्यद्वस्तेः समं भेषजमस्ति यस्मात्
lines_iast: tasyātivṛddhasya śamāyaṃ nānyadvasteḥ samaṃ bheṣajamasti yasmāt

hindi: वायु पर यत्न से विजय पाने पर उससे प्रेरित पित्त, कफ आदि भी शान्त हो जाते हैं।
english: And when the wind (anila) is conquered with effort, the Pitta, Kapha and the rest stirred by it are also pacified.
notes: Completes the 'yasmāt' clause of 139. 'anila' is a synonym of vāyu (wind).
lines_deva: शाम्यंति यत्नेन जिते ऽनिले च तदीरिताः पित्तकफादयोऽपि
lines_iast: śāmyaṃti yatnena jite 'nile ca tadīritāḥ pittakaphādayo'pi

hindi: इसलिए वे कहते हैं कि चिकित्सा का आधा; कोई कोई बस्ति को सम्पूर्ण चिकित्सा भी कहते हैं।
english: Therefore they say 'half of treatment'; some (say) basti (is) even the whole treatment.
notes: Elliptical: the verb 'bruvanti' is carried into the second half, and the first object is not named (basti, by context). 'cikitsārddham' printed with doubled dd, normalised to 'ardham'.

hindi: और जो पक्वाशय में स्थित होता हुआ भी दोषों को पैर से सिर तक
english: And that which, though staying in the pakvāśaya (seat of the digested), the doṣas from foot to head
notes: GROUPING: the sentence continues in 143, which gives the verb 'ādatte' (draws) and the subject basti; no verb is supplied here. pakvāśaya = the seat of the digested, the lower abdomen/large intestine (standard).

hindi: बस्ति वीर्य यानी शक्ति से उन्हें खींच लेता है, स्वस्थ सूर्य के भूमि के रसों को खींचने की भाँति।
english: The basti draws (them) by (its) potency (vīrya), like the healthy sun the juices of the earth.
notes: Verb for 142 ('doṣān'). 'svastha' is literally 'healthy, in good condition' and is not further interpreted. The object 'them' is supplied from 142 (doṣān).

hindi: जो वहाँ औषध का वीर्य यानी शक्ति है, वह निश्चय ही अपान वायु के द्वारा
english: Which is the potency (vīrya) of the drug there, that indeed by the apāna wind (apāna-vāyu)

text_flags.why: possible: tat + apānena with 'a' dropped in print; metre and sense fit

notes: GROUPING: the sentence continues in 145. No verb is supplied. 'tadpānena' is read as 'tat apānena'; the metre (8 syllables) agrees.

hindi: पूर्ण रूप से शीघ्र ही समान वायु प्राप्त कर लेता है।
english: Fully, very soon, the samāna (wind) obtains (it).
notes: Completes the sentence of 144; the object 'it' (the drug's potency) is understood from 144. samāna is one of the five winds (vāyu).

hindi: समान के बाद इसी प्रकार व्यान आदि वायु क्रम से।
english: And thus, after samāna, the winds beginning with vyāna, in order.
notes: No verb in this unit; 147 supplies it ('yānti') for the winds. 'vyānādyāḥ' = those beginning with vyāna.

hindi: वे, अनुमानित पाठ के अनुसार तूमाः अस्पष्ट, अपनी प्रकृति को जाते हैं, शरीर के अनुग्रह में स्थित।
english: They, on a conjectural reading 'tūmāḥ' (unclear), go to their natural state, standing in the support (anugraha) of the body.
notes: 'tūmāḥ' cannot be restored: perhaps 'ūṣmāṇaḥ/ūṣmāḥ' (hot ones) or 'tūrṇam' (quickly), neither sure; kept as printed. 'te' = the winds of 146. 'prakṛtim yānti' is read as 'go to their natural state'.
lines_deva: ते तूमाः प्रकृतिं यांति शरीरानुग्रहे स्थिताः
lines_iast: te tūmāḥ prakṛtiṃ yāṃti śarīrānugrahe sthitāḥ

hindi: बलपूर्वक पित्त और श्लेष्म को दबाकर और यथास्थान स्थापित करके
english: Having overpowered, and having placed in their own places, Pitta and phlegm (śleṣman),

text_flags.why: possible: 'praisahya' is not a word; 'prasahya' (having overpowered/forcibly) fits; metre also

notes: GROUPING: continues in 149 (verb 'santarpayanti'). 'praisahya' is read as 'prasahya' (ai for a, possible typo).

hindi: वे शरीर में अपने अपने भूतगुणों को चारों ओर से तृप्त करते हैं।
english: They nourish all around their own respective qualities of the bhūtas (elements or beings) in the body.
notes: The subject is the winds of 146-147. 'bhūta' is kept as the Sanskrit term; 'elements' is the usual sense in this context (probable) but the text does not say. 'svān svān' means 'each its own'.

hindi: व्यान तिरछा, अपान नीचे और प्राण ऊपर खींचता है।
english: Vyāna draws crosswise, apāna downward, and prāṇa upward.
notes: The verb 'prakarṣati' is singular and shared by the three subjects. The object (the drug's potency, understood) is not stated.

hindi: अपने अपने ही अनुसार, वहन करने वाली नाड़ियों से जल की भाँति।
english: Each according to its own, as water through carrying channels (nāḍī).
notes: No verb in this unit; it follows from 150. 'udakam' is a comparison ('like water').

words.gram: ppp. caus. su-√yuj, m. nom. sg.

hindi: इस प्रकार अथवा उनसे और सिराओं से, शरीर को, सुप्रयुक्त बस्ति
english: Thus, or by those and by the sirās (vessels), the body, the well-applied basti
notes: GROUPING: continues in 153 ('vyāpnuvan ... hanti'): the body is the object of 'vyāpnuvan'. 'taiḥ' (by those) has no clear referent (masculine; perhaps the nāḍīs of 151), so the line is rendered literally.
lines_deva: एवं वा तैः सिराभिश्च वपुर्बस्तिः सुयोजितः
lines_iast: evaṃ vā taiḥ sirābhiśca vapurbastiḥ suyojitaḥ

words.gram: pres. part. vi-√āp, m. nom. sg.

hindi: व्याप्त होता हुआ बलपूर्वक अत्यन्त कष्टसाध्य यक्ष्मन् यानी क्षय रोगों को भी नष्ट करता है।
english: Pervading (it), it forcibly destroys even the very difficult yakṣmans (wasting diseases).
notes: Completes 152; 'it' is the basti. 'yakṣmaṇaḥ' is accusative plural in masculine form (taken as masculine, agreeing with 'sukṛcchrān'). Hindi gives 'यक्ष्मन् यानी क्षय रोग' per glossary (yakṣman = wasting disease, consumption; tuberculosis-type is probable).

hindi: इसलिए बस्ति सब कर्मों में प्रधान है और सब का अन्त करने वालों को सम्पूर्ण रूप से नष्ट करता है।
english: Therefore basti is the chief of all procedures (karman), and it destroys the all-ending (ones) completely.
notes: 'sarvāntakān' is rendered literally 'all-ending (ones)'; what is meant (deadly diseases?) is not stated in the text and is not added. 'pradhānam' is neuter though 'bastiḥ' is masculine (predicate nouns). 'karma' = treatment procedures.

hindi: और स्रोत के भीतर शुद्ध करके, दोषों, तेज, शुक्र, देह और अग्नि की दीप्ति करे।
english: And having cleansed within the channel (srotas), it would make the doṣas, tejas (brilliance), and the brightness of semen (śukra), body and digestive fire (agni).

text_flags.why: possible: extra 'mi' in print; 'dīptim iti' intended

notes: Difficult: 'doṣān' may be the object of 'śodhayitvā' (having cleansed the doṣas) rather than of 'kuryāt'; the word order puts it after 'kuryāt', and the literal reading is kept. 'tejaḥ' is read as a separate item and 'dīptim' as brightness of the group. The printed 'dīptimimiti' has an extra 'mi' (read 'dīptim iti'). 'strotas' is the printed spelling of srotas. The closing 'iti' ends the quotation.

hindi: इस प्रकार सिद्धबस्तिकल्प नामक पञ्चम अध्याय।
english: Thus the fifth chapter, named Siddhabastikalpa (the preparations of the 'siddha' basti).
notes: GROUPING: chapter colophon (typed as a verse in the input), not a verse. 'siddha' in the title is kept as in the text ('accomplished'; the title means the basti preparations).
